question: persister

ideas.title: Rose-moles in stipple: mapping the pre-treatment expression tail
ideas.description: Use single-molecule RNA FISH (or amplified clampFISH) against candidate resistance drivers across millions of untreated cells, then treat and re-image the identical field to test whether survivors came from the rare high-expressing 'stippled' subpopulation. This quantifies how much of survival is explained by the tail of each gene's distribution rather than its mean.

ideas.title: Who knows how?: resolving the kinetic origin of the rare state
ideas.description: Measure transcriptional bursting of the candidate driver gene using intronic FISH or live MS2/PP7 reporters to determine whether rare high-expressing cells arise from increased burst frequency, larger burst size, or slow mRNA/protein turnover. Then perturb each parameter via promoter swaps or degron tags and test whether survivor frequency shifts accordingly.

ideas.title: Swift, slow: live-imaging linkage of division kinetics to survival fate
ideas.description: Track thousands of single cells through drug addition with FUCCI cell-cycle reporters plus death and division readouts, retrospectively linking each survivor's pre-treatment cycle length and signaling dynamics to its outcome. This distinguishes persistence through quiescence from persistence through active bypass signaling, which have opposite therapeutic implications.

ideas.title: Landscape plotted and pieced: spatial neighborhood versus cell-intrinsic causes
ideas.description: Grow cells at controlled densities and in spatially resolved colonies, then use spatial transcriptomics or imaging mass cytometry to test whether survivors cluster in local patches (indicating paracrine or contact-mediated protection) rather than scattering at random. Follow up with targeted neighbor ablation and conditioned-media swaps to establish causality.

ideas.title: All trades, their gear and tackle: cataloguing distinct survivor programs and their heritability
ideas.description: Profile survivors with single-cell multiome (RNA + ATAC) and phospho-CyCIF to test whether they occupy one state or several distinct bypass-pathway programs requiring different combination therapies. Pair this with heritable lineage barcoding and split-and-retreat experiments to measure how long each primed state persists and whether it is re-inducible, identifying the invariant epigenetic generator behind the variable states.
